why: 7706 -> 7713, +7 bytes, for the whole of text selection: typing, Backspace and Delete all
replace a live range, and both offsets are clamped rather than trusted.
Seven bytes because the three editing branches collapsed into one. Insert, Backspace and
Delete were separate splices, and over a range they are provably the same operation --
measured, and the surprise is that Backspace and Delete become *identical* once a range is
live, neither taking the extra character its collapsed behaviour would. So the erase
direction only widens a collapsed caret by one, and everything else is `replace [from, to)`.
A first pass kept the branches and added a fourth for the range: +289 bytes, over the
ratchet, which is how the unification got found.
Re-blessed at the exact figure rather than left inside the +2% tolerance, for the reason the
previous entry gives: slack nobody wrote down is charged to whoever changes this next.
Nothing per frame, and nothing about the selection itself: the anchor, the focus, the word
boundaries and the drag all live in `caret.rs`, so a Shift+Arrow and a pointer drag cost no
runtime bytes and no round trip. The 7 is the price of splicing on this side.
